content: Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of idelalisib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly decrease systemic exposure to idelalisib, necessitating close monitoring. Phenobarbital increases the effects of ifosfamide by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism, which may enhance the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active metabolite. This can increase the formation of neurotoxic and nephrotoxic metabolites, such as chloroacetaldehyde. Use caution and monitor closely for toxicities, considering dose adjustments. Iloperidone enhances the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic synergy, while belladonna alkaloids reduce iloperidone levels via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Phenobarbital and iloperidone both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids also reduce iloperidone levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, applicable only to oral forms. Phenobarbital decreases iloperidone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces imatinib levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. This interaction is minor but requires close monitoring. Phenobarbital and imipramine both increase sedation, while belladonna alkaloids and imipramine reduce cholinergic effects. Phenobarbital decreases imipramine levels by inducing CYP1A2, CYP2C19, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Barbiturates may increase adverse effects, such as respiratory depression, with toxic doses of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs). Therapeutic doses of TCAs may have reduced blood concentrations due to increased metabolism by barbiturates. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces indinavir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital significantly reduces the levels or effects of infigratinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Belladonna alkaloids and ipratropium both reduce cholinergic effects. Due to poor systemic absorption of ipratropium, interactions are unlikely at recommended dosages. Phenobarbital reduces iptacopan levels by inducing CYP2C8 metabolism, potentially reducing its efficacy. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital significantly reduces irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Phenobarbital is contraindicated with isavuconazonium sulfate due to significant reduction in its levels via CYP3A4 induction. Phenobarbital reduces isosorbide dinitrate and isosorbide mononitrate levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Phenobarbital reduces isradipine levels via CYP3A4 induction, though the significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital significantly reduces levels or effects of istradefylline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Phenobarbital reduces itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 induction and inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption, applicable only to oral forms. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces ivabradine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Phenobarbital significantly reduces ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 induction, leading to a ~9-fold reduction in systemic exposure. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Phenobarbital reduces ivermectin levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital significantly reduces ivosidenib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Phenobarbital reduces ixabepilone levels or effects via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital significantly reduces ixazomib levels via CYP3A4 induction, decreasing Cmax by 54% and AUC by 74%. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Phenobarbital and ixekizumab interactions are influenced by cytokine-mediated alterations in CYP450 enzyme formation during chronic inflammation. Ixekizumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme formation. Monitor therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing ixekizumab in patients on concomitant CYP450 substrates. Kava enhances phenobarbital effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and ketamine both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces ketoconazole levels via CYP3A4 induction and inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption, applicable only to oral forms. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital and ketotifen (ophthalmic) both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. L-methylfolate reduces phenobarbital levels by increasing metabolism, while phenobarbital reduces L-methylfolate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, applicable only to oral forms. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces labetalol levels by increasing metabolism. Consider higher beta-blocker doses during co-administration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces lansoprazole levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 induction. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces lapatinib levels via CYP3A4 induction and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital significantly reduces larotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. If co-administration is unavoidable, double the larotrectinib dose and resume the prior dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inducer for 3-5 half-lives. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital and lasmiditan both increase sedation. Co-administration with other CNS depressants, including alcohol, has not been evaluated. Lasmiditan may cause sedation and other cognitive or neuropsychiatric adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital is contraindicated with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir due to significant reduction in sofosbuvir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity, decreasing conversion to its active metabolite responsible for 90% of its pharmacologic effect. Phenobarbital significantly reduces lefamulin levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers unless benefits outweigh risks. Monitor for reduced efficacy. Phenobarbital and lemborexant both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Phenobarbital significantly reduces lenacapavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Phenobarbital significantly reduces leniolisib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Phenobarbital reduces lesinurad levels via CYP2C9/10 induction. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Phenobarbital significantly reduces letermovir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid co-administration with P-gp inducers. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while levalbuterol decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. Phenobarbital reduces levamlodipine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Monitor blood pressure closely when co-administered with CYP3A4 inducers. Phenobarbital and levetiracetam both increase sedation. Limit use to patients for whom alternative treatments are inadequate. Phenobarbital reduces levocarnitine levels via an unspecified mechanism. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital and levocetirizine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Belladonna alkaloids may enhance levodopa effects but exacerbate tardive dyskinesia. High doses of anticholinergics may reduce levodopa effects by delaying gastrointestinal absorption. Phenobarbital reduces levoketoconazole levels via CYP3A4 induction and inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption, applicable only to oral forms. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces levonorgestrel levels (intrauterine and oral) via CYP3A4 induction. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; use alternative or backup contraception during and for 28 days after discontinuing enzyme inducers. Phenobarbital and levorphanol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces levothyroxine levels by increasing metabolism. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces lidocaine levels via CYP1A2 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces linagliptin levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and strongly consider alternative treatments.
